description:
Service Management and Orchestration Framework Diagram Caption

The diagram illustrates the Service Management and Orchestration Framework for an ORAN and 5G network. It shows various components and their interactions as follows:

1. "Software Package Onboarding" from the "Software Package Onboarding" component to the "Service Management and Orchestra" component.
2. "Service & Slice Subnet Orchestration" from "Service & Slice Subnet Orchestration" to the "Service Management and Orchestra" component.
3. "Topology & Inventory Management" from "Topology & Inventory Management" to the "Service Management and Orchestra" component.
4. "AI/ML Workflow" from "AI/ML Workflow" to the "Service Management and Orchestra" component.
5. "Data Management and Exposure" from "Data Management and Exposure" to the "Service Management and Orchestra" component.
6. "Service Management and Exposure" from "Service Management and Exposure" to the "Service Management and Orchestra" component.
7. "Policy Management and Information" from "Policy Management and Information" to the "Service Management and Orchestra" component.
8. "Open FH M-plane" from "Software Package Onboarding," "Service & Slice Subnet Orchestration," and "Topology & Inventory (TE&IV)" components to the "O-Cloud" component.
9. "Open FH M-plane" to the "O-RU" component via "RAN NF OAM (e.g., CM, NF, FM, Tracing, Logging, etc.)" from "Federated O-Cloud Management and Orchestration (FOCOM)" and "Policy Management and Information (PMI)" components.
10. "SMOS Communication" from "O-Cloud" to "SMOOS" from left to right across various components including "SMOS Producer" and "SMO Producer anchored in Non-RT R RC".
12. "SMOS Communication" from "Policy Management and Information" to "rApp Management" via "Non-RT RIC SMOSO" communication in reverse flow.
13. "Service Management and Exposure" from "Service Management and Exposure" to "SMOS Producer" and "SMM Producer" components.
14. "KM/ML Workflow" from "AI/ML Workflow" to "SMM Producer."
15. "Data Management and Exposure" from "Data Management and Exposure" to "SMM Producer."
16. "KSMO Producer" to any "SMM Producer anchored in Non-RT R I" through "SMSM Producer to SMCMO Producer."

text: The SMOS Communication, shown in Figure 4.1-1, represents the logical support for communication between any SMOS Producer, SMOS Consumer, and rApps. Examples of SMOS Communication implementation include, but are not limited to, service mesh, API gateway, direct communication, and message bus. SMOS consumers and producers rely on the capabilities provided by SME for purposes such as service discovery and on the capabilities provided by DME for purposes such as data exposure.

text: The R1 interface, shown in Figure 4.1-1, is a service-based interface. R1 termination, also shown in Figure 4.1-1, enables R1 service producers and R1 service consumers to exchange messages via the R1 interface.

text: In a service-based SMO architecture, the SME can be leveraged as a generic SMOS, handling service management and exposure for any SMOSs within SMO. The SME SMOS provides a set of common SMO capabilities that are needed for all SMO Services.
trace: 4.2 SMO Services \(SMOS\) --> 4.2.2 Service Management and Exposure \(SME\) SMOS description
text_preview: In a service-based SMO architecture, the SME can be leveraged as a generic SMOS, handling service management and exposure for any SMOSs within SMO. The SME SMOS provides a set of common SMO capabilities that are needed for all SMO Services.

text: The SME SMOS offers the following capabilities:
trace: 4.2 SMO Services \(SMOS\) --> 4.2.2 Service Management and Exposure \(SME\) SMOS description
text_preview: The SME SMOS offers the following capabilities:

text:
* Service registration,
  * Service discovery,
  * Authentication and authorization to access a service,
  * Communication support \(e.g. service mesh\) between Service Producers and Service Consumers,
  * Bootstrap of new Service consumers and Service Producers \(determination of the endpoints for the SME services\) \(optional\),
  * Heartbeat of Service producers \(optional\).
trace: 4.2 SMO Services \(SMOS\) --> 4.2.2 Service Management and Exposure \(SME\) SMOS description
text_preview:
* Service registration
* Service discovery
* Authentication and authorization
* Communication support (e.g., service mesh)
* Bootstrap of new consumers and producers (determination of endpoints, optional)
* Optional: Heartbeat of Service Producers

text: The role of one, or both, of Service Producer and Service Consumer can be assumed by any SMOF or rApp in the SMO. The services are registered individually. The Service Consumers can also be external to the SMO, for the services made discoverable and exposed also to the external SMO consumers.

text: 4.2.3 Data Management and Exposure \(DME\) SMOS description
trace: 4.2 SMO Services \(SMOS\) --> 4.2.2 Service Management and Exposure \(SME\) SMOS description --> 4.2.3 Data Management and Exposure \(DME\) SMOS description
text_preview: 4.2.3 Data Management and Exposure \(DME\) SMOS description

text: The DME SMOS provides capabilities that allow Data Consumers, as defined in the Non-RT RIC Architecture specification \[i.1\], to discover data types and to consume collected data, and allow Data Producers, as defined in the Non-RT RIC Architecture specification \[i.1\], to register data types and to produce data for collection. The DME services can handle any registered data types and expose them for discovery and consumption to Data Consumers. In the Non-RT RIC Architecture specification \[i.1\] clause 3.2, both the Data Producer and Data Consumer are restricted to refer only to rApps, because the scope of \[i.1\] is the R1 interface between rApps and the SMO/Non-RT RIC framework.
trace: 4.2 SMO Services \(SMOS\) --> 4.2.2 Service Management and Exposure \(SME\) SMOS description --> 4.2.3 Data Management and Exposure \(DME\) SMOS description
text_preview: The DME SMOS provides capabilities for Data Consumers to discover data types and consume collected data, and for Data Producers to register and produce data. DME services handle registered data types, exposing them for discovery and consumption by Data Consumers.

text: This is extended in a decoupled service-based SMO architecture, where the DME SMOS can be leveraged as an enabler handling any SMOS data types, therefore any SMOF can also be a Data Producer and/or a Data Consumer which can benefit from using DME SMOS to register, produce, discover and consume data.
trace: 4.2 SMO Services \(SMOS\) --> 4.2.2 Service Management and Exposure \(SME\) SMOS description --> 4.2.3 Data Management and Exposure \(DME\) SMOS description
text_preview: In a decoupled service-based SMO architecture, the DME SMOS enables handling of various SMOS data types. As an enabler, it allows any SMOF to be both a Data Producer and Consumer, benefiting from its registration, production, discovery, and consumption capabilities.

text: The role of one, or both, of Data Producer and Data Consumer can be assumed by any SMOF and rApp \(for the data types related to each SMOS and/or rApp\) in the SMO. The SMO Data Consumers can also be external SMO consumers, for the data made discoverable and allowed to be exposed to the external SMO consumers.
trace: 4.2 SMO Services \(SMOS\) --> 4.2.2 Service Management and Exposure \(SME\) SMOS description --> 4.2.3 Data Management and Exposure \(DME\) SMOS description
text_preview: The role of one or both Data Producer and Consumer can be assumed by any SMOF and rApp for related data types in the SMO. SMO Data Consumers can also be external, accessing discoverable data made available to them.

text: The RAN NF OAM SMOS includes, but is not limited to, the following set of capabilities:

text_preview: The RAN NF OAM SMOS includes, but is not limited to, the following set of capabilities:

text:
* Provisioning Management, including bulk and basic synchronous and asynchronous configuration management CRUD \(create, read, update, delete\) operations, CM notifications and model exposure.
  * Fault Supervision Management, including alarm subscription, notification, clearing, acknowledgement, and query
  * Performance Management, including PM counter initiation and supervision
  * Trace Management, including trace initiation and supervision
  * Streaming Data Reporting, including stream collection and stream exposure.
  * File Data Reporting, including file collection and file exposure.
  * PNF software and hardware management.

text: 4.2.5 Network Function Orchestrator SMOS description
trace: 4.2.4 RAN NF OAM SMOS description --> 4.2.5 Network Function Orchestrator SMOS description
text_preview: 4.2.5 Network Function Orchestrator SMOS description

text: The Network Function Orchestrator \(NFO\) SMOS includes capabilities for the orchestration of the NF Deployments that constitute the Cloudified NFs. This includes the initial deployment of the software and any subsequent lifecycle management actions necessary on the respective NF Deployments instances, such as healing, updates, scaling, software upgrades, termination, etc.

text_preview: The Network Function Orchestrator (NFO) SMOS includes capabilities for orchestrating NF deployments that constitute Cloudified NFs. It covers initial deployment and lifecycle management actions, including healing, updates, scaling, upgrades, termination, and others.

text: 4.2.6 Federated O-Cloud Orchestration and Management \(FOCOM\) SMOS description

text: The Federated O-Cloud Orchestration and Management \(FOCOM\) SMOS includes capabilities for orchestration of cluster and infrastructure resources in one or several O-Clouds. It includes, but is not limited to, the following capabilities:
trace: 4.2.4 RAN NF OAM SMOS description --> 4.2.6 Federated O-Cloud Orchestration and Management \(FOCOM\) SMOS description
text_preview: The Federated O-Cloud Orchestration and Management \(FOCOM\) SMOS includes capabilities for orchestration of cluster and infrastructure resources in one or several O-Clouds. It includes, but is not limited to, the following capabilities:

text:
* Querying and discovery of O-Cloud infrastructure inventory information such as O-Cloud Sites, physical and logical infrastructure resources, Node Clusters, Deployment Managers and O-Cloud Template information.
  * Subscription for notifications related to changes in O-Cloud infrastructure inventory information.
  * Provisioning \(create, update, delete\) of cluster and infrastructure resources in each O-Cloud.
  * Monitoring of cluster and infrastructure resources in each O-Cloud.
trace: 4.2.4 RAN NF OAM SMOS description --> 4.2.6 Federated O-Cloud Orchestration and Management \(FOCOM\) SMOS description
text_preview:
Querying and discovery of O-Cloud infrastructure info, including sites, nodes, clusters, and templates.
Subscription for notifications on changes to O-Cloud inventory.
Provisioning (create, update, delete) of cluster and infrastructure resources.
Monitoring of cluster and infrastructure resources in each O-Cloud.

text: The FOCOM SMOS exposes O-Cloud infrastructure inventory information that is acquired from the O-Cloud O2ims inventory service. The FOCOM SMOS enables the service consumer to subscribe for notifications related to particular O-Cloud resource types.

text: 4.2.7 Service and Slice Subnet Orchestration SMOS \(SO SMOS\) description
trace: 4.2.4 RAN NF OAM SMOS description --> 4.2.6 Federated O-Cloud Orchestration and Management \(FOCOM\) SMOS description --> 4.2.7 Service and Slice Subnet Orchestration SMOS \(SO SMOS\) description
text_preview: 4.2.7 Service and Slice Subnet Orchestration SMOS \(SO SMOS\) description

text: The SO SMOS includes capabilities to perform the orchestration of a RAN service and/or slice subnet. This includes both the orchestration of the fulfilment of the RAN service or the RAN slice subnet, and orchestration support for the actuation of an assurance process. The behaviour of the SO SMOS is dependent on both the SO requests that it receives and the related artifacts to support the requests. The exact definition of the RAN service is defined by the operator using the SMO, it can be generally considered as a logical concept that represents the capability for the RAN within a certain geographic area, to provide UEs the ability to have voice and/or data connectivity to the core, with requested characteristics. This includes the RAN slice subnet. In order to execute on its responsibilities, the SO SMOS consumes other services including the RAN NF OAM SMOS for configuration, the FOCOM SMOS for infrastructure management requests, the NFO for deployment requests, as well as services produced by rApps, etc.
trace: 4.2.4 RAN NF OAM SMOS description --> 4.2.6 Federated O-Cloud Orchestration and Management \(FOCOM\) SMOS description --> 4.2.7 Service and Slice Subnet Orchestration SMOS \(SO SMOS\) description
text_preview: the so orchestrates ran service and / or slice subnet , including orchestration of fulfilment and actuation of assurance processes . its behavior depends on received requests and related artifacts . the operator defines the ran service concept , representing voice / data connectivity within a geographic area , consuming services like nf oam smos to execute its responsibilities

text: The SO SMOS includes the following capabilities:
trace: 4.2.4 RAN NF OAM SMOS description --> 4.2.6 Federated O-Cloud Orchestration and Management \(FOCOM\) SMOS description --> 4.2.7 Service and Slice Subnet Orchestration SMOS \(SO SMOS\) description
text_preview: The SO SMOS includes the following capabilities:

text:
* Oversees and automates the fulfillment of a service or a slice subnet order, received directly or via a higher -level orchestrator, according to the information contained in the service or a slice subnet order and the related artifacts, utilizing the services provided by SMOFs \(such as SMOFs supporting RAN NF OAM SMOS for configuration, NFO SMOS for NF Deployment \[2\] LCM, etc.\) and services produced by rApps.
  * Coordinates the orchestration of lifecycle and service or the slice subnet-related configuration for one or more RAN NFs \(also including multiple NF Deployments\), including taking the homing decision considering both the RAN service or the slice subnet, and application-level requirements as well as the non-functional requirements e.g., infrastructure capabilities needed as well as the transport networks used to interconnect the O-RAN NFs \(and NF Deployments\) and O-RUs when they are deployed over different sites in order to meet the connectivity requirements for the RAN service or the slice subnet. This can include generating the required configuration used when requesting \(via the appropriate SMOS\) the configuration of the RAN NFs.
  * Coordination of the NFs transport connectivity: based on requirements and objectives obtained on RAN NF connectivity it requests the suitable transport networks management domain to fulfil the requirements of the RAN service and/or slice subnet requirements.
  * Based on the infrastructure requirements of the O-RAN NF Deployments, it orchestrates the necessary management actions to the O-Cloud infrastructure, by coordinating with FOCOM SMOS producer for the needed O-Cloud management requests.

text: The SA SMOS includes the following capabilities:
trace: 4.2.8 Service and Slice Subnet Assurance SMOS \(SA SMOS\) description
text_preview: The SA SMOS includes the following capabilities:

text:
* Assures the intended state \(together with rApps and/or other SMOSs\) of the RAN services and slice subnets.
  * It monitors/observes the data that is relevant \(produced by other SMOS producers and/or services produced by rApps\) to assessing the current RAN service, and/or RAN slice subnet characteristics against the service requirements.
  * In case the RAN service and/or RAN slice subnet requirements are not met, decisions are taken \(together with rApps and/or other SMOSs\) on a course of remedial actions.
trace: 4.2.8 Service and Slice Subnet Assurance SMOS \(SA SMOS\) description
text_preview: Monitors RAN services and slice subnets to ensure they meet requirements. It observes data from relevant producers/services to assess current characteristics against service needs. If requirements aren't met, decisions are made with rApps and/or other SMOSs on remedial actions.

text: 4.2.9 rApp Management SMOS description

text: The rApp management SMOS includes the following set of capabilities:
trace: 4.2.8 Service and Slice Subnet Assurance SMOS \(SA SMOS\) description --> 4.2.9 rApp Management SMOS description
text_preview: The rApp management SMOS includes the following set of capabilities:

text:
* rApp lifecycle management, including rApp deployment, rApp upgrade and rApp termination.
  * rApp configuration management, which enables management of the rApp instance configuration settings.
  * rApp fault management, which enables an rApp instance to report faults that are related to the rApp itself or to its communication with other entities.
  * rApp performance management, which enables an rApp instance to report on the performance of the rApp itself or to its communication with other entities.
  * rApp logging, which enables an rApp instance to generate and report timestamped logs, including audit trail records of its configuration actions within the network.
trace: 4.2.8 Service and Slice Subnet Assurance SMOS \(SA SMOS\) description --> 4.2.9 rApp Management SMOS description
text_preview:
Lifecycle management includes deployment, upgrade, and termination of rApps. This covers:

* Configuration management for rApp settings
* Fault management for reporting rApp-related issues
* Performance management for monitoring rApp performance
* Logging for generating timestamped logs and audit trail records.
